title: Supreme Court: Mitchell v. Wisconsin
summary: The Wisconsin Supreme Court’s judgment—affirming the drunk-driving convictions of petitioner Mitchell, who was administered a warrantless blood test while he was unconscious—is vacated, and the case is remanded. (No. 18-6210, opinion by Justice Alito; 588 U.S. 840).

title: Supreme Court: Department of Commerce v. New York
summary: The Secretary did not violate the Enumeration Clause or the Census Act in deciding to reinstate a citizenship question on the 2020 census questionnaire, but the District Court was warranted in remanding the case back to the agency where the evidence tells a story that does not match the Secretary’s explanation for his decision. (No. 18-966, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 588 U.S. 752).

title: Supreme Court: Rucho v. Common Cause
summary: Partisan gerrymandering claims present political questions beyond the reach of the federal courts. (No. 18-422, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 588 U.S. 684).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Haymond
summary: The Tenth Circuit’s judgment—that 18 U. S. C. §3583(k)’s last two sentences are unconstitutional and unenforceable—is vacated, and the case is remanded. (No. 17-1672, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 588 U.S. 634).

title: Supreme Court: Kisor v. Wilkie
summary: Auer v. Robbins, 519 U. S. 452, and Bowles v. Seminole Rock & Sand Co., 325 U. S. 410—under which deference is given to an agency’s reasonable reading of its own genuinely ambiguous regulations—are not overruled. (No. 18-15, opinion by Justice Kagan; 588 U.S. 558).

title: Supreme Court: Tennessee Wine and Spirits Retailers Assn. v. Thomas
summary: Tennessee’s 2-year durational-residency requirement applicable to retail liquor store license applicants violates the Commerce Clause and is not saved by the Twenty-first Amendment. (No. 18-96, opinion by Justice Alito; 588 U.S. 504).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Davis
summary: Title 18 U. S. C. §924(c)(3)(B), which provides enhanced penalties for using a firearm during a “crime of violence,” is unconstitutionally vague. (No. 18-431, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 588 U.S. 445).

title: Supreme Court: Food Marketing Institute v. Argus Leader Media
summary: Where commercial or financial information is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner and provided to the government under an assurance of privacy, the information is “confidential” within the meaning of 5 U. S. C. §552(b)(4), the Freedom of Information Act’s Exemption 4. (No. 18-481, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 588 U.S. 427).

title: Supreme Court: Iancu v. Brunetti
summary: The Lanham Act prohibition on the registration of “immoral” or “scandalous” trademarks infringes the First Amendment. (No. 18-302, opinion by Justice Kagan; 588 U.S. 388).

title: Supreme Court: Dutra Group v. Batterton
summary: A plaintiff may not recover punitive damages on a maritime claim of unseaworthiness. (No. 18-266, opinion by Justice Alito; 588 U.S. 358).

title: Supreme Court: Flowers v. Mississippi
summary: The trial court at Flowers’ sixth murder trial committed clear error in concluding that the State’s peremptory strike of a particular black prospective juror was not motivated in substantial part by discriminatory intent. (No. 17-9572, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 588 U.S. 284).

title: Supreme Court: North Carolina Dept. of Revenue v. Kimberley Rice Kaestner 1992 Family Trust
summary: The presence of in-state beneficiaries alone does not empower a State to tax trust income that has not been distributed to the beneficiaries where the beneficiaries have no right to demand that income and are uncertain to receive it. (No. 18-457, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 588 U.S. 262).

title: Supreme Court: Rehaif v. United States
summary: In a prosecution under 18 U. S. C. §922(g) and §924(a)(2), the Government must prove both that the defendant knew he possessed a firearm and that he knew he belonged to the relevant category of persons barred from possessing a firearm. (No. 17-9560, opinion by Justice Breyer; 588 U.S. 225).

title: Supreme Court: Knick v. Township of Scott
summary: A government violates the Takings Clause when it takes property without compensation, and a property owner may bring a Fifth Amendment claim under 42 U. S. C. §1983 at that time; the state-litigation requirement of Williamson County Regional Planning Comm’n v. Hamilton Bank of Johnson City, 473 U. S. 172, is overruled. (No. 17-647, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 588 U.S. 180).

title: Supreme Court: Gundy v. United States
summary: The Second Circuit’s judgment that 34 U. S. C. §20913(d)—which requires the Attorney General to apply the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act’s registration requirements as soon as feasible to offenders convicted before the statute’s enactment—is not an unconstitutional delegation of legislative authority is affirmed. (No. 17-6086, opinion by Justice Kagan; 588 U.S. 128).

title: Supreme Court: McDonough v. Smith
summary: The statute of limitations for McDonough’s 42 U. S. C. §1983 fabricated-evidence claim against his prosecutor began to run when the criminal proceedings against him terminated in his favor—that is, when he was acquitted at the end of his second trial. (No. 18-485, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 588 U.S. 109).

title: Supreme Court: American Legion v. American Humanist Assn.
summary: The Bladensburg Cross does not violate the Establishment Clause. (No. 17-1717, opinion by Justice Alito; 588 U.S. 29).

title: Supreme Court: PDR Network, LLC v. Carlton Harris Chiropractic, Inc.
summary: The extent to which a 2006 FCC Order interpreting the term “unsolicited advertisement” binds lower courts may depend on the resolution of two preliminary questions that the Fourth Circuit should address in the first instance: (1) whether the Order is the equivalent of a legislative rule, which has the force and effect of law, or an interpretative rule, which does not; and (2) whether petitioners had a “prior” and “adequate” opportunity to seek judicial review of the Order. (No. 17-1705, opinion by Justice Breyer; 588 U.S. 1).

title: Supreme Court: Manhattan Community Access Corp. v. Halleck
summary: Petitioner, a private nonprofit corporation designated by New York City to operate the public access channels on the Manhattan cable system owned by Time Warner (now Charter), is not a state actor subject to the First Amendment. (No. 17-1702, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 587 U.S. 802).

title: Supreme Court: Virginia Uranium, Inc. v. Warren
summary: The Fourth Circuit’s judgment that the Atomic Energy Act does not preempt Virginia’s prohibition on uranium mining in the Commonwealth is affirmed. (No. 16-1275, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 587 U.S. 761).

title: Supreme Court: Gamble v. United States
summary: The dual sovereignty doctrine—under which two offenses are not the “same offence” for double jeopardy purposes if prosecuted by separate sovereigns—is upheld. (No. 17-646, opinion by Justice Alito; 587 U.S. 678).

title: Supreme Court: Virginia House of Delegates v. Bethune-Hill
summary: The House of Delegates lacks standing to appeal the invalidation of Virginia’s redistricting plan. (No. 18-281, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 587 U.S. 658).

title: Supreme Court: Quarles v. United States
summary: Michigan’s third-degree home-invasion statute substantially corresponds to or is narrower than generic burglary for purposes of qualifying for enhanced sentencing under the Armed Career Criminal Act. (No. 17-778, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 587 U.S. 645).

title: Supreme Court: Return Mail, Inc. v. Postal Service
summary: The Federal Government is not a “person” capable of petitioning the Patent Trial and Appeal Board to institute patent review proceedings under the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act. (No. 17-1594, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 587 U.S. 618).

title: Supreme Court: Parker Drilling Management Services, Ltd. v. Newton
summary: Under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, where federal law addresses the relevant issue, state law is not adopted as surrogate federal law on the Outer Continental Shelf. (No. 18-389, opinion by Justice Thomas; 587 U.S. 601).

title: Supreme Court: Azar v. Allina Health Services
summary: Because the Department of Health and Human Services neglected its statutory notice-and-comment obligations when it revealed a new policy that dramatically—and retroactively—reduced Medicare payments to hospitals serving low-income patients, its policy must be vacated. (No. 17-1484, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 587 U.S. 566).

title: Supreme Court: Taggart v. Lorenzen
summary: A creditor may be held in civil contempt for violating a bankruptcy court’s discharge order if there is no fair ground of doubt as to whether the order barred the creditor’s conduct. (No. 18-489, opinion by Justice Breyer; 587 U.S. 554).

title: Supreme Court: Fort Bend County v. Davis
summary: The charge-filing precondition to suit set out in Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 is not a jurisdictional requirement. (No. 18-525, opinion by Justice Ginsburg; 587 U.S. 541).

title: Supreme Court: Mont v. United States
summary: Pretrial detention later credited as time served for a new conviction tolls a supervised-release term under 18 U. S. C. §3624(e), even if the court must make the tolling calculation after learning whether the time will be credited. (No. 17-8995, opinion by Justice Thomas; 587 U.S. 514).
